misconception_description: Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.

solutions.generated_code:
program HapusSpasi
kamus
  s, hasil : string
  i : integer
algoritma
  inputBaris(s)
  hasil <- ""
  i <- 1
  if i <= panjang(s) then
    if s[i] != ' ' then
      hasil <- hasil + s[i]
    endif
    i <- i + 1
  endif
  output(hasil)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student rewrites the solution using an if-statement that removes only one whitespace at a time using replace with a count of 1. The student genuinely believes that the if-statement will continue executing as long as there are spaces in text1, repeatedly removing spaces until none remain (like a while loop would). In reality, the if-statement executes only once, removing just the first space, and then the function returns the incompletely processed string. This demonstrates the misconception that if-statements loop while their condition is true.
